title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
title_zh: 社交碎片化前，亚洲象种群流动增加及群体孤立
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.
abstract_zh: 人类和许多其他动物都生活在对生存和福祉至关重要的相互联系的社会群体中。原则上，群体在组成成员发生变化的情况下仍可持续存在。然而，成员变化的逐步积累可能将系统推过临界阈值，进入另一种状态，重新结构化连接模式。此类变化还会影响系统抵抗干扰的韧性。我们对443只野生雌性亚洲象在12年内的社会网络动态进行了研究，追踪其群体成员身份和结构。在积累的人口流动之后，网络分裂为更小且更孤立的社群。连接的变化不仅源于成员的丧失，还源于剩余个体之间关系的修正。这为长寿陆生哺乳动物社会网络在经历逐步积累的人口流动后出现持久状态改变提供了经验证据。
